subject.title: Bug: Telegram delivery queue recovery can replay old sendMessage replies and duplicate delivery-mirror transcript entries

question: How should OpenClaw treat legacy pending Telegram outbound queue rows that lack `recoveryState` after migration?
rationale: Source inspection shows old rows can still bypass the new no-blind-replay guard, but the right upgrade behavior trades off duplicate sends against possibly dropping a pending delivery.

options.title: Quarantine ambiguous legacy rows
options.body: Move legacy Telegram rows without `recoveryState` to failed or a reviewable quarantine during migration so startup never blindly resends them.

options.title: Keep ambiguous rows pending
options.body: Mark legacy rows as `unknown_after_send` and leave them pending until a Telegram reconciliation path can prove whether the send landed.

options.title: Allow legacy blind replay
options.body: Preserve current replay behavior for old rows and accept the duplicate-message risk for pre-migration queues.

recommendation.title: Quarantine ambiguous legacy rows
recommendation.body: Move legacy Telegram rows without `recoveryState` to failed or a reviewable quarantine during migration so startup never blindly resends them.

likelyOwner.reason: They most recently worked on the ambiguous-send recovery state path that this migration policy must align with.
